extension.summary: An evolving world of digital creatures: glowing cell bodies that graze, hunt, bud offspring and mutate
extension.description:
A screensaver after ALIEN, the artificial life simulator: a world of digital creatures, each a small body of glowing cells held together by elastic connections and built cell by cell from its genome. Sensors look for food or prey, muscles bend, crawl or push the body towards it, digestors turn the energy particles that radiation sources emit into life, attackers steal energy from creatures of other lineages and defenders blunt their attacks; reconnectors grab prey or hold on to rocks, injectors write their genome into other creatures like a virus, detonators blast their neighbours away, depots store energy for lean times, and memory and communicator cells keep and share signals. A well-fed creature builds an offspring at its tail, cell by cell, and sets it free with a copy of its genome that may have mutated: a new cell type, a different bend, a rewired neural network, now and then a new colour. Nobody tells them what to become; the energy is limited, so the ones that gather it best spread and the others die out, and what you see after half an hour is not what the world started with.
Bodies are wriggling worms, stiff ribbons, rings, flowers, filled hexagonal jellies and tadpoles. Four worlds: Grazers, Grazers and hunters (with red predators among them), a Primordial soup of random genomes left to sort themselves out, and an Ecosystem of every design with hunters, puffers and viruses. Grey rocks give the world some geography. A new world fades in every 20 minutes, or never.
The organic look follows ALIEN's renderer: the bodies are drawn as soft, fused, translucent tissue with relief lighting, a membrane rim and a wet sheen, over a dim nebula, with bloom, glowing energy particles and radiation sources, attack and injection beams, detonation flashes and shock waves. The camera shows the whole world, tours the busiest places or follows one creature after another. A classic look of glowing cells and lines is still there.
The settings cover the world (which one, size, energy, mutation rate, number of radiation sources, rocks, muscle strength, how often a new world starts), the look (organic or classic, camera, colour by genome as ALIEN does, by cell type, by lineage or by energy; cell size; bloom; connections; energy particles; the sources' glow; events; motion trails; dim) and the performance (picture resolution, speed, threads).
The simulation runs on the CPU and is built to be light, like Dancing Boids and Emergence: cells in fixed slots, a contact grid rebuilt every step by counting sort, a contact, bond and movement pass split over up to four cores with results identical to one, creature logic once per 6-step cycle, and the organic layers drawable at half resolution for weak GPUs.
extension.disclaimer: This is a native add-on: it is built per platform and Kodi version (this one: Kodi 21 Omega on macOS, Intel and Apple Silicon, and 64-bit Android). It needs OpenGL or OpenGL ES 2.0. Inspired by ALIEN by Christian Heinemann (https://github.com/chrxh/alien, BSD 3-Clause); this is an independent, much smaller CPU simulation with its own renderer and settings, and contains no ALIEN code.
extension.news: 2.0.0 - an organic look after ALIEN's renderer (soft shaded, fused bodies, bloom, nebulae, attack beams, detonation shock waves), a camera that tours or follows creatures, six new cell types (depot, injector, reconnector, detonator, memory, communicator), muscles that bend and crawl, hexagonal jellies and tadpoles, rocks, and an Ecosystem world 1.0.0 - initial release
